mutations.name: a skipped case is reported as passed
mutations.comment: Silent skipping, the anti-goal #2866 names first. The run stays green and the counts line still totals, so only a test asserting the SKIPPED state separates a case that was declined from one that passed.

mutations.name: cleanup runs in written order instead of reverse
mutations.comment: Step reordering. A teardown written beside the setup it undoes stops being correct, and a fixture whose cleanups are independent passes either way -- the committed one drops two tables with a foreign key between them. slices.All rather than a bare range: it iterates forward with the same two-value shape, so the mutation changes the ORDER and nothing else -- dropping the call would leave the import unused and measure nothing.

mutations.name: cleanup is omitted when the case body failed
mutations.comment: Cleanup omission. The case still fails for its own reason, so the verdict is unchanged; only asserting that the cleanup step APPEARS on a failing case catches it.

mutations.name: an expanded case evaluates against the base context, losing each and self
mutations.old:
ctx := atlasEvalContext(
			caseContext.variables, instance, iteration, caseContext.options)
mutations.comment: Expression-context loss. The case still expands, the instances are still named correctly and the count is right -- every per-instance assertion short of comparing the STATEMENTS passes.

mutations.name: an external step in a cleanup bypasses the authorization
mutations.comment: External opt-in bypass, and this one shipped: a case holds its steps in two slices and the guard walked one, so an unauthorized program ran from a teardown. The test asserts the program's SIDE EFFECT, because an error alone does not say it was never started.
